display.title: Episode 343: The Storyteller, Chapter 6 (Chai Elul)
display.summary_short: On Chai Elul: the Hakochainik march, Rabbi Yehuda's one remembered story begins, Shema with a first-grade class, a listener's letter, and the boyhood of the Baal Shem Tov.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the evening of Chai Elul 5748. Uncle Yossi recalls that in Elul Hashem, the King in the field, smiles at everyone, so Tzivos Hashem soldiers answer with simcha and the Hakochainik march. In the story, Rabbi Yehuda begins the one story he remembers: the Baal Shem Tov once took him to a city ruled by a feared official who issued harsh decrees against the Jews, and sent him straight to that official's office to demand a meeting. As Rabbi Yehuda knocks on the door, the chapter breaks off. A first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema, and in the mailbox a young listener who wrote the whole Shema from memory is signed up for Tzivos Hashem. After a sponsor message, Uncle Yossi marks the Baal Shem Tov's birthday with a story from his childhood: orphaned at five, little Yisroelik remembers his father's last words, 'Fear nothing but Hashem alone', studies alone in a forest cave, and tells a radiant old stranger he is never alone, because Hashem is with him; the stranger becomes his teacher.
display.lesson: Fear nothing and no one but Hashem; one who knows Hashem is with him is never alone.

date.note: 'Tonight is Chai Elul' on a Tuesday night: the eve of 18 Elul, Tuesday 30 August 1988; matches the weekly estimate.
